newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico says pipeline builders to spend $240 mln.
newsitem.headline: Mexico says pipeline builders to spend $240 mln.

text.p: The winning bidders to construct the Yucatan state Merida III natural gas pipeline plan to spend about $240 million on the project, Mexico's Federal Electricity Commission (CFE) said on Thursday.

Canada's largest pipeline company, TransCanada Pipelines Ltd., led a consortium with U.S.-based International Generating Co. (InterGen) and private Mexican builder Gutsa Construcciones. TransCanada holds 62.5 percent of the bid, InterGen holds 32.5 percent and Gutsa holds 5 percent.
TransCanada, however, said the consortium expects to spend between $250 million and $300 million on the project.

The pipeline will be 24 inches wide and 700 km (437 miles) long, with operations expected to begin in the third quarter of 1999, the CFE said in a statement. About 10.4 million cubic feet of natural gas per day should travel the pipeline, it added.

The Yucatan state pipeline will supply natural gas to Merida III, Mexico's first private power plant. AES Corp., Japan's Nichimen Corp and Grupo Hermes won the five-year operating concession for the 440-megawatt plant in late January, expected to begin operating by 2000.
"The project...will supply the fuel to the (plant), in addition to other CFE plants in Campeche and Yucatan states," CFE said.
The pipeline will run from Ciudad Pemex in Tabasco state to Valladolid, Yucatan state.

Mexico is in the process of auctioning private concessions to build new power plants throughout the country, which should accelerate in the second quarter, Energy Minister Jesus Reyes Heroles recently told reporters.

Other bidders for the pipeline project were: Gasoductos Enron de Yucatan; Nova Corporation with The Williams Companies Inc. and Perez Companc International Limited; Bufete Industrial with Shell Oil Co. and Mitsui & Co. Ltd. ; and Epic Yucatan with Gas del Sur, Constructora ICA and Snam Spa.
